topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the opening framing and sets expectations for studying the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the complement cascade
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the foundational architecture, nomenclature conventions, and core biochemical properties of the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the mechanisms by which the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways trigger complement activation on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the downstream processes through which complement eliminates pathogens and stimulates inflammation.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the inhibitory mechanisms and regulatory proteins that prevent complement-mediated destruction of host tissue.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the distinct pathological consequences and disease presentations associated with deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement immunity
topics.groupedBecause: It details the evolutionary mechanisms and molecular strategies used by pathogens to subvert complement clearance.

topics.label: Conclusion and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: It provides concluding remarks for the session and introduces the upcoming topic.
